or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

### Syntax

#### Recognized shapes

The following shapes are recognized by `ditaa`:

- **Document** `{d}`: A shape with a wavy bottom edge
- **Storage** `{s}`: A cylindrical shape (database-like)
- **Ellipse** `{o}`: An oval/ellipse shape
- **Manual operation** `{mo}`: A shape with a slanted top
- **Decision** `{c}` ("Choice"): A diamond shape
- **Trapezoid** `{tr}`: A trapezoid shape
- **Input/Output** `{io}`: A parallelogram shape

Example:

```
+--------+   
|{d}     |   
|        |   
+--------+

`ditaa` recognizes color codes:

- `cRED` - Red
- `cGRE` - Green
- `cBLU` - Blue
- `cPNK` - Pink
- `cYEL` - Yellow
- `cBLK` - Black

    84	
    85	### Syntax
    86	
    87	#### Recognized shapes
    88	
    89	The following shapes are recognized by `ditaa`:
    90	
    91	- **Document** `{d}`: A shape with a wavy bottom edge
    92	- **Storage** `{s}`: A cylindrical shape (database-like)
    93	- **Ellipse** `{o}`: An oval/ellipse shape
    94	- **Manual operation** `{mo}`: A shape with a slanted top
    95	- **Decision** `{c}` ("Choice"): A diamond shape
    96	- **Trapezoid** `{tr}`: A trapezoid shape
    97	- **Input/Output** `{io}`: A parallelogram shape
    98	
    99	Example:
   100	
   101	```
   102	+--------+   
   103	|{d}     |   
   104	|        |   
   105	+--------+   
   106	```
   107	
   108	![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/document.png)
   109	
   110	#### Color
   111	
   112	`ditaa` recognizes color codes:
   113	
   114	- `cRED` - Red
   115	- `cGRE` - Green
   116	- `cBLU` - Blue
   117	- `cPNK` - Pink
   118	- `cYEL` - Yellow
   119	- `cBLK` - Black
   120	
   121	Example:
   122	
   123	```
   124	+---------+
   125	| cBLU    |
   126	|         |
   127	|    +----+
   128	|    |cPNK|
   129	|    |    |
   130	+----+----+
   131	```
   132	
   133	![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/color.png)
   134	
   135	Common edge separation (default):
   136	
   137	![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/separation.png)
   138	
   139	No separation (with the `-E` option):
   140	
   141	![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/no_separation.png)
   142	
   143	#### Dashed lines
   144	
   145	Any lines that contain either at least one `=` (for horizontal lines) or at least one `:` (for vertical lines) are rendered as dashed lines. Only one of those characters can make a whole line dashed, so this feature "spreads". The rationale behind this is that you only have to change one character to switch from normal to dashed line, and vice versa.
   146	
   147	Example:
   148	
   149	```
   150	----+  /----\  +----+
   151	    :  |    |  :    |
   152	    |  |    |  |{s} |
   153	    v  \-=--+  +----+
   154	```
   155	
   156	![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/dashed_demo.png)
   157	
   158	#### Point markers
   159	
   160	If `*` is encountered on a line (but not at the end of the line), it is rendered as a special marker, called the point marker. Example:
   161	
   162	```
   163	*----*
   164	|    |      /--*
   165	*    *      |
   166	|    |  -*--+
   167	*----*
   168	```
   169	
   170	![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/point_marker.png)
   171	
   172	#### Text handling
   173	
   174	If the pattern ' o XXXXX' is encountered, where XXXXX is any text, the 'o' is interpreted and rendered as a bullet point. Note that there must be a space before the 'o' as well as after it.
   175	
   176	Example:
   177	
   178	```
   179	/-----------------\
   180	| Things to do    |
   181	| cGRE            |
   182	| o Cut the grass |
   183	| o Buy jam       |
   184	| o Fix car       |
   185	| o Make website  |
   186	\-----------------/
   187	```
   188	
   189	![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/bullet.png)
   190	
   191	#### HTML mode
   192	
   193	When `ditaa` is run using the `--html` option, the input is an HTML file. The contents of the `
` tags are rendered as diagrams and saved in the images directory and a new HTML file is produced with the appropriate `` tags.
   194	
   195	If the id parameter is present in the `
` tag, its value is used as the filename of the rendered png. Otherwise a filename of the form `ditaa_diagram_X.png` is used, where X is a number.
   196	
   197	In this mode, files that exist are not generated again, they are just skipped. You can force overwrite of the files using the `--overwrite` option.
   198	
   199	## License

   202

{"command":"set +e
rm -rf /tmp/ditaabg && mkdir /tmp/ditaabg
cat > /tmp/ditaabg/a.txt <<'EOF'
x
EOF
for args in '' '-b FF0000' '-b 80FF0000' '-T' '-T -b FF0000' '-b BAD' '-b FFFFF' '-b FFFFFF00' '-b ff00aa'; do
 name=$(echo "$args"|tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9_' ); [ -z "$name" ] && name=default
 echo "### $args"
 ./executable /tmp/ditaabg/a.txt /tmp/ditaabg/$name.png $args > /tmp/ditaabg/$name.out 2>/tmp/ditaabg/$name.err; c=$?; echo exit=$c; cat /tmp/ditaabg/$name.out | sed -n '1,20p'; echo stderr:; cat /tmp/ditaabg/$name.err
 if [ -f /tmp/ditaabg/$name.png ]; then python3 - <<PY
import struct,zlib
p='/tmp/ditaabg/$name.png'; data=open(p,'rb').read(); print('sig',data[:8]); print('ihdr',struct.unpack('>IIBBBBB',data[16:29]));
# decompress first pixel
pos=8; idat=b''
while pos<len(data):
 l=struct.unpack('>I',data[pos:pos+4])[0]; typ=data[pos+4:pos+8];
 if typ==b'IDAT': idat+=data[pos+8:pos+8+l]
 pos+=12+l
raw=zlib.decompress(idat); print('raw_first',list(raw[:10]))
PY
 fi
done"}

actions.command:
cat > ditaa_reimpl.py <<'PY' #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Small from-scratch ditaa-compatible command line renderer. This implementation is intentionally self-contained: it parses the documented command line, recognises common ASCII-art boxes/connectors/markup, and writes PNG/SVG output without third-party libraries. """ from __future__ import annotations import codecs import math import os import re import struct import sys import time import zlib from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple VERSION_BANNER = "\nditaa version 0.11, Copyright (C) 2004--2017 Efstathios (Stathis) Sideris\n" HELP_UPPER = """usage: java -jar ditaa.jar [OUTFILE] [-A] [-b ] [-d] [-E] [-e ] [-h] [--help] [-o] [-r] [-S] [-s ] [--svg] [--svg-font-url ] [-T] [-t ] [-v] [-W] -A,--no-antialias Turns anti-aliasing off. -b,--background The background colour of the image. The format should be a six-digit hexadecimal number (as in HTML, FF0000 for red). Pass an eight-digit hex to define transparency. This is overridden by --transparent. -d,--debug Renders the debug grid over the resulting image. -E,--no-separation Prevents the separation of common edges of shapes. -e,--encoding The encoding of the input file. -h,--html In this case the input is an HTML file. The contents of the 
 tags are rendered as
                                diagrams and saved in the images directory
                                and a new HTML file is produced with the
                                appropriate  tags.
    --help                      Prints usage help.
 -o,--overwrite                 If the filename of the destination image
                                already exists, an alternative name is
                                chosen. If the overwrite option is
                                selected, the image file is instead
                                overwriten.
 -r,--round-corners             Causes all corners to be rendered as round
                                corners.
 -S,--no-shadows                Turns off the drop-shadow effect.
 -s,--scale              A natural number that determines the size
                                of the rendered image. The units are
                                fractions of the default size (2.5 renders
                                1.5 times bigger than the default).
    --svg                       Write an SVG image as destination file.
    --svg-font-url        SVG font URL.
 -T,--transparent               Causes the diagram to be rendered on a
                                transparent background. Overrides
                                --background.
 -t,--tabs                Tabs are normally interpreted as 8 spaces
                                but it is possible to change that using
                                this option. It is not advisable to use
                                tabs in your diagrams.
 -v,--verbose                   Makes ditaa more verbose.
 -W,--fixed-slope               Makes sides of parallelograms and
                                trapezoids fixed slope instead of fixed
                                width.
"""
HELP_LOWER = HELP_UPPER.replace(" [OUTFILE]", " [outfile]", 1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Command line parsing

NOARG_SHORT = {
    "A": "no-antialias",
    "d": "debug",
    "E": "no-separation",
    "h": "html",
    "o": "overwrite",
    "r": "round-corners",
    "S": "no-shadows",
    "T": "transparent",
    "v": "verbose",
    "W": "fixed-slope",
}
ARG_SHORT = {
    "b": "background",
    "e": "encoding",
    "s": "scale",
    "t": "tabs",
}
NOARG_LONG = {v: k for k, v in NOARG_SHORT.items()}
NOARG_LONG.update({"help": None, "svg": None})
ARG_LONG = {
    "background": "b",
    "encoding": "e",
    "scale": "s",
    "tabs": "t",
    "svg-font-url": None,
}
DISPLAY_ORDER_NAME = {
    "no-antialias": "no-antialias",
    "debug": "debug",
    "no-separation": "no-separation",
    "html": "html",
    "overwrite": "overwrite",
    "round-corners": "round-corners",
    "no-shadows": "no-shadows",
    "transparent": "transparent",
    "verbose": "verbose",
    "fixed-slope": "fixed-slope",
    "help": "help",
    "svg": "svg",
    "background": "background",
    "encoding": "encoding",
    "scale": "scale",
    "tabs": "tabs",
    "svg-font-url": "svg-font-url",
}

class ParseError(Exception):
    pass

@dataclass
class ParsedOptions:
    opts: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]]
    positionals: List[str]

    def has(self, name: str) -> bool:
        return any(n == name for n, _ in self.opts)

    def first(self, name: str, default: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
        for n, v in self.opts:
            if n == name:
                return v
        return default


def looks_like_known_option(token: str) -> bool:
    if token == "--":
        return True
    if token.startswith("--") and len(token) > 2:
        name = token[2:].split("=", 1)[0]
        return name in NOARG_LONG or name in ARG_LONG or True  # Apache treats --xxx as an option here
    if token.startswith("-") and len(token) > 1:
        ch = token[1]
        return ch in NOARG_SHORT or ch in ARG_SHORT
    return False


def parse_command_line(argv: Sequence[str]) -> ParsedOptions:
    opts: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = []
    pos: List[str] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if tok == "--":
            pos.extend(argv[i + 1 :])
            break
        if tok.startswith("--") and len(tok) > 2:
            raw = tok[2:]
            if "=" in raw:
                name, value = raw.split("=", 1)
            else:
                name, value = raw, None
            if name in NOARG_LONG:
                # Commons CLI accepts --flag and, for our purposes, ignores an =value.
                opts.append((name, None))
            elif name in ARG_LONG:
                if value is None:
                    if i + 1 >= len(argv) or looks_like_known_option(argv[i + 1]):
                        short = ARG_LONG[name] or name
                        raise ParseError(f"Missing argument for option: {short}")
                    i += 1
                    value = argv[i]
                opts.append((name, value))
            else:
                raise ParseError(f"Unrecognized option: --{name}")
        elif tok.startswith("-") and len(tok) > 1:
            j = 1
            while j < len(tok):
                ch = tok[j]
                if ch in NOARG_SHORT:
                    opts.append((NOARG_SHORT[ch], None))
                    j += 1
                    continue
                if ch in ARG_SHORT:
                    name = ARG_SHORT[ch]
                    if j + 1 < len(tok):
                        value = tok[j + 1 :]
                        opts.append((name, value))
                        j = len(tok)
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= len(argv) or looks_like_known_option(argv[i + 1]):
                            raise ParseError(f"Missing argument for option: {ch}")
                        i += 1
                        opts.append((name, argv[i]))
                        j = len(tok)
                    continue
                raise ParseError(f"Unrecognized option: -{ch}")
        else:
            pos.append(tok)
        i += 1
    return ParsedOptions(opts, pos)


def print_help(upper: bool = True) -> None:
    sys.stdout.write(HELP_UPPER if upper else HELP_LOWER)


def option_lines(parsed: ParsedOptions) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    for name, value in parsed.opts:
        if name == "help":
            continue
        if value is None:
            lines.append(DISPLAY_ORDER_NAME.get(name, name))
        else:
            lines.append(f"{DISPLAY_ORDER_NAME.get(name, name)} = {value}")
    return lines

# Diagram analysis data

@dataclass
class Shape:
    r1: int
    c1: int
    r2: int
    c2: int
    kind: str = "rect"
    fill: Color = WHITE
    text: Color = BLACK
    dashed: bool = False

@dataclass
class LineSeg:
    x1: float
    y1: float
    x2: float
    y2: float
    dashed: bool = False

@dataclass
class Arrow:
    x: float
    y: float
    direction: str

@dataclass
class Marker:
    x: float
    y: float

@dataclass
class TextRun:
    row: int
    col: int
    text: str
    color: Color

@dataclass
class DiagramModel:
    lines: List[str]
    rows: int
    cols: int
    scale: float
    cw: int
    ch: int
    width: int
    height: int
    shapes: List[Shape]
    segs: List[LineSeg]
    arrows: List[Arrow]
    markers: List[Marker]
    texts: List[TextRun]
    debug: bool

    def cx(self, c: float) -> float:
        return math.floor((2.0 + c + 0.5) * self.cw)

    def cy(self, r: float) -> float:
        return math.floor((2.0 + r + 0.5) * self.ch)


def expand_tabs(text: str, tabsize: int) -> str:
    if "\t" in text and tabsize <= 0:
        raise ZeroDivisionError("/ by zero")
    return "\n".join(line.expandtabs(tabsize) for line in text.split("\n"))


def shape_bounds(shape: Shape, model: DiagramModel) -> Tuple[float, float, float, float]:
    return model.cx(shape.c1), model.cy(shape.r1), model.cx(shape.c2), model.cy(shape.r2)


def in_bounds(grid: List[List[str]], r: int, c: int) -> bool:
    return 0 <= r < len(grid) and 0 <= c < (len(grid[0]) if grid else 0)


def find_shapes(lines: List[str], rows: int, cols: int) -> Tuple[List[Shape], List[List[bool]]]:
    grid = [list(line.ljust(cols)) for line in (lines if lines else [""] * rows)]
    consumed = [[False] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
    shapes: List[Shape] = []

    def ch(r: int, c: int) -> str:
        return grid[r][c] if in_bounds(grid, r, c) else " "

    corner = set("+*")

    def h_ok(r: int, c1: int, c2: int) -> bool:
        if c2 <= c1:
            return False
        saw = False
        for c in range(c1 + 1, c2):
            if ch(r, c) not in "-=+*":
                return False
            if ch(r, c) in "-=":
                saw = True
        return saw or c2 == c1 + 1

    def v_ok(c: int, r1: int, r2: int) -> bool:
        if r2 <= r1:
            return False
        saw = False
        for r in range(r1 + 1, r2):
            if ch(r, c) not in "|:+*":
                return False
            if ch(r, c) in "|:":
                saw = True
        return saw or r2 == r1 + 1

    candidates: List[Shape] = []
    for r1 in range(rows):
        for c1 in range(cols):
            if ch(r1, c1) not in corner:
                continue
            for c2 in range(c1 + 2, cols):
                if ch(r1, c2) not in corner or not h_ok(r1, c1, c2):
                    continue
                for r2 in range(r1 + 2, rows):
                    if ch(r2, c1) in corner and ch(r2, c2) in corner and h_ok(r2, c1, c2) and v_ok(c1, r1, r2) and v_ok(c2, r1, r2):
                        candidates.append(Shape(r1, c1, r2, c2))
                        break  # prefer the nearest bottom for this top edge
    # Prefer larger outer shapes for drawing, but avoid exact duplicates.
    seen = set()
    candidates.sort(key=lambda s: ((s.r2 - s.r1) * (s.c2 - s.c1), s.r1, s.c1), reverse=True)
    for s in candidates:
        key = (s.r1, s.c1, s.r2, s.c2)
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        # Avoid tiny boxes wholly inside an already detected one unless they have their own border.
        shapes.append(s)

    marker_order = ["{mo}", "{tr}", "{io}", "{d}", "{s}", "{o}", "{c}"]
    marker_kind = {"{mo}": "manual", "{tr}": "trapezoid", "{io}": "io", "{d}": "document", "{s}": "storage", "{o}": "ellipse", "{c}": "decision"}

    for s in shapes:
        # Dashed outlines spread across the whole outline.
        outline_chars = []
        for c in range(s.c1, s.c2 + 1):
            outline_chars.append(ch(s.r1, c)); outline_chars.append(ch(s.r2, c))
        for r in range(s.r1, s.r2 + 1):
            outline_chars.append(ch(r, s.c1)); outline_chars.append(ch(r, s.c2))
        s.dashed = any(c in "=:" for c in outline_chars)
        # Mark boundary consumed.
        for c in range(s.c1, s.c2 + 1):
            consumed[s.r1][c] = True; consumed[s.r2][c] = True
        for r in range(s.r1, s.r2 + 1):
            consumed[r][s.c1] = True; consumed[r][s.c2] = True
        # Markup search in the interior.
        for r in range(s.r1 + 1, s.r2):
            rowtxt = "".join(grid[r][s.c1 + 1 : s.c2])
            for code, (fill, txt) in COLOR_CODES.items():
                idx = rowtxt.find(code)
                if idx >= 0:
                    s.fill, s.text = fill, txt
                    for k in range(len(code)):
                        cc = s.c1 + 1 + idx + k
                        if 0 <= cc < cols:
                            consumed[r][cc] = True
                    break
            for mark in marker_order:
                idx = rowtxt.find(mark)
                if idx >= 0:
                    s.kind = marker_kind[mark]
                    for k in range(len(mark)):
                        cc = s.c1 + 1 + idx + k
                        if 0 <= cc < cols:
                            consumed[r][cc] = True
                    break
    return shapes, consumed


def analyse_diagram(text: str, opts: ParsedOptions) -> DiagramModel:
    scale_s = opts.first("scale", "1") or "1"
    try:
        scale = float(scale_s)
    except Exception:
        scale = 1.0
    tabs_s = opts.first("tabs", "8") or "8"
    try:
        tabsize = int(tabs_s)
    except Exception:
        tabsize = 8
    text = expand_tabs(text, tabsize)
    raw_lines = text.splitlines()
    rows = len(raw_lines) if raw_lines else 1
    cols = max((len(l) for l in raw_lines), default=0)
    cw = int(10 * scale)
    ch = int(14 * scale)
    if cw <= 0:
        cw = 1
    if ch <= 0:
        ch = 1
    width = (cols + 4) * cw
    height = (rows + 4) * ch
    lines = [l.ljust(cols) for l in raw_lines]
    if not lines:
        lines = ["".ljust(cols)]
    shapes, consumed = find_shapes(lines, rows, cols)
    grid = [list(line.ljust(cols)) for line in lines]

    model = DiagramModel(lines, rows, cols, scale, cw, ch, width, height, shapes, [], [], [], [], opts.has("debug"))

    def char(r: int, c: int) -> str:
        if 0 <= r < rows and 0 <= c < cols:
            return grid[r][c]
        return " "

    # Bullet markers (space-o-space) are text features.
    bullet_positions: set[Tuple[int, int]] = set()
    for r in range(rows):
        for m in re.finditer(r" o (?=\S)", lines[r]):
            c = m.start() + 1
            if c < cols and not consumed[r][c]:
                bullet_positions.add((r, c))
                consumed[r][c] = True
                x, y = model.cx(c), model.cy(r)
                model.markers.append(Marker(x, y))

    # Arrows.
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            if consumed[r][c]:
                continue
            cc = char(r, c)
            if cc in "<>^v":
                model.arrows.append(Arrow(model.cx(c), model.cy(r), cc))
                consumed[r][c] = True

    # Point markers.
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            if char(r, c) == "*":
                model.markers.append(Marker(model.cx(c), model.cy(r)))
                consumed[r][c] = True

    # Horizontal line runs.
    hchars = set("-=+*")
    for r in range(rows):
        c = 0
        while c < cols:
            if (char(r, c) in hchars and not consumed[r][c]) or char(r, c) in "-=":
                start = c
                dashed = char(r, c) == "="
                while c + 1 < cols and (char(r, c + 1) in hchars or char(r, c + 1) in "<>") and not (char(r, c + 1) in "|:"):
                    c += 1
                    dashed = dashed or char(r, c) == "="
                end = c
                if end > start:
                    model.segs.append(LineSeg(model.cx(start), model.cy(r), model.cx(end), model.cy(r), dashed))
                    for cc in range(start, end + 1):
                        if char(r, cc) in hchars:
                            consumed[r][cc] = True
            c += 1

    # Vertical line runs.
    vchars = set("|:+*")
    for c in range(cols):
        r = 0
        while r < rows:
            if (char(r, c) in vchars and not consumed[r][c]) or char(r, c) in "|:":
                start = r
                dashed = char(r, c) == ":"
                while r + 1 < rows and (char(r + 1, c) in vchars or char(r + 1, c) in "^v"):
                    r += 1
                    dashed = dashed or char(r, c) == ":"
                end = r
                if end > start:
                    model.segs.append(LineSeg(model.cx(c), model.cy(start), model.cx(c), model.cy(end), dashed))
                    for rr in range(start, end + 1):
                        if char(rr, c) in vchars:
                            consumed[rr][c] = True
            r += 1

    # Diagonal strokes.
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            if consumed[r][c]:
                continue
            cc = char(r, c)
            x0 = (2 + c) * model.cw
            y0 = (2 + r) * model.ch
            if cc == "/":
                model.segs.append(LineSeg(x0, y0 + model.ch, x0 + model.cw, y0, False))
                consumed[r][c] = True
            elif cc == "\\":
                model.segs.append(LineSeg(x0, y0, x0 + model.cw, y0 + model.ch, False))
                consumed[r][c] = True

    # Text runs.  Remove diagram syntax/control characters; preserve internal spaces.
    control = set("+-=|:/\\<>^v*")

    def text_color_for(r: int, c: int) -> Color:
        for s in shapes:
            if s.r1 < r < s.r2 and s.c1 < c < s.c2:
                return s.text
        return BLACK

    for r in range(rows):
        clean = []
        for c in range(cols):
            cc = char(r, c)
            if consumed[r][c] or cc in control:
                clean.append(" ")
            else:
                clean.append(cc)
        row = "".join(clean)
        # Split into runs separated by two or more spaces.
        c = 0
        while c < cols:
            while c < cols and row[c] == " ":
                c += 1
            if c >= cols:
                break
            start = c
            last_non = c
            gap = 0
            while c < cols:
                if row[c] == " ":
                    gap += 1
                    if gap >= 2:
                        # If there is non-space later, break; otherwise trim at end.
                        if any(chh != " " for chh in row[c + 1 :]):
                            break
                else:
                    gap = 0
                    last_non = c
                c += 1
            txt = row[start : last_non + 1]
            if txt:
                model.texts.append(TextRun(r, start, txt, text_color_for(r, start)))
            if gap >= 2:
                c += 1
    return model

# Raster canvas and PNG writer

class Canvas:
    def __init__(self, w: int, h: int, bg: Color):
        self.w = max(1, int(w))
        self.h = max(1, int(h))
        self.p = bytearray(self.w * self.h * 4)
        r, g, b, a = bg
        for i in range(0, len(self.p), 4):
            self.p[i] = r; self.p[i + 1] = g; self.p[i + 2] = b; self.p[i + 3] = a

    def blend(self, x: int, y: int, col: Color) -> None:
        if x < 0 or y < 0 or x >= self.w or y >= self.h:
            return
        r, g, b, a = col
        idx = (y * self.w + x) * 4
        if a >= 255:
            self.p[idx] = r; self.p[idx + 1] = g; self.p[idx + 2] = b; self.p[idx + 3] = 255
            return
        if a <= 0:
            return
        da = self.p[idx + 3]
        inv = 255 - a
        nr = (r * a + self.p[idx] * inv) // 255
        ng = (g * a + self.p[idx + 1] * inv) // 255
        nb = (b * a + self.p[idx + 2] * inv) // 255
        na = min(255, a + da * inv // 255)
        self.p[idx] = nr; self.p[idx + 1] = ng; self.p[idx + 2] = nb; self.p[idx + 3] = na

    def disk(self, cx: float, cy: float, rad: float, col: Color) -> None:
        r = max(0.5, rad)
        x0 = int(math.floor(cx - r)); x1 = int(math.ceil(cx + r))
        y0 = int(math.floor(cy - r)); y1 = int(math.ceil(cy + r))
        rr = r * r
        for y in range(y0, y1 + 1):
            for x in range(x0, x1 + 1):
                if (x + 0.5 - cx) ** 2 + (y + 0.5 - cy) ** 2 <= rr:
                    self.blend(x, y, col)

    def line(self, x1: float, y1: float, x2: float, y2: float, col: Color, width: float = 1.0, dashed: bool = False) -> None:
        dx, dy = x2 - x1, y2 - y1
        length = max(1.0, math.hypot(dx, dy))
        steps = max(1, int(length * 2))
        dash_len = 5.0
        radius = max(0.55, width / 2.0)
        for i in range(steps + 1):
            t = i / steps
            if dashed:
                dist = t * length
                if int(dist // dash_len) % 2 == 1:
                    continue
            self.disk(x1 + dx * t, y1 + dy * t, radius, col)

    def polygon(self, pts: List[Tuple[float, float]], fill: Optional[Color], stroke: Optional[Color] = None, width: float = 1.0, dashed: bool = False) -> None:
        if fill is not None and len(pts) >= 3:
            minx = max(0, int(math.floor(min(x for x, _ in pts))))
            maxx = min(self.w - 1, int(math.ceil(max(x for x, _ in pts))))
            miny = max(0, int(math.floor(min(y for _, y in pts))))
            maxy = min(self.h - 1, int(math.ceil(max(y for _, y in pts))))
            for y in range(miny, maxy + 1):
                yy = y + 0.5
                xs = []
                for i in range(len(pts)):
                    x1, y1 = pts[i]
                    x2, y2 = pts[(i + 1) % len(pts)]
                    if (y1 <= yy < y2) or (y2 <= yy < y1):
                        if y2 != y1:
                            xs.append(x1 + (yy - y1) * (x2 - x1) / (y2 - y1))
                xs.sort()
                for a, b in zip(xs[0::2], xs[1::2]):
                    for x in range(max(minx, int(math.floor(a))), min(maxx, int(math.ceil(b))) + 1):
                        self.blend(x, y, fill)
        if stroke is not None:
            for i in range(len(pts)):
                x1, y1 = pts[i]
                x2, y2 = pts[(i + 1) % len(pts)]
                self.line(x1, y1, x2, y2, stroke, width, dashed)

    def ellipse(self, cx: float, cy: float, rx: float, ry: float, fill: Optional[Color], stroke: Optional[Color], width: float = 1.0) -> None:
        if rx <= 0 or ry <= 0:
            return
        x0 = max(0, int(cx - rx - width)); x1 = min(self.w - 1, int(cx + rx + width))
        y0 = max(0, int(cy - ry - width)); y1 = min(self.h - 1, int(cy + ry + width))
        for y in range(y0, y1 + 1):
            for x in range(x0, x1 + 1):
                v = ((x + 0.5 - cx) / rx) ** 2 + ((y + 0.5 - cy) / ry) ** 2
                if fill is not None and v <= 1.0:
                    self.blend(x, y, fill)
                if stroke is not None and abs(v - 1.0) <= max(0.08, width / max(rx, ry)):
                    self.blend(x, y, stroke)

    def text(self, x: int, y: int, s: str, col: Color, scale: float) -> None:
        pix = max(1, int(round(2 * scale)))
        # Keep characters within the 10*scale cell advance.
        adv = max(1, int(10 * scale))
        cx = x
        for ch in s:
            glyph = FONT_5X7.get(ch) or FONT_5X7.get(ch.upper()) or ["11111", "10001", "00010", "00100", "00100", "00000", "00100"]
            for gy, row in enumerate(glyph):
                for gx, bit in enumerate(row):
                    if bit == "1":
                        for yy in range(pix):
                            for xx in range(pix):
                                self.blend(cx + gx * pix + xx, y + gy * pix + yy, col)
            cx += adv


def png_bytes(canvas: Canvas, rgb_only: bool) -> bytes:
    def chunk(t: bytes, d: bytes) -> bytes:
        return struct.pack(">I", len(d)) + t + d + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(t + d) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    color_type = 2 if rgb_only else 6
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", canvas.w, canvas.h, 8, color_type, 0, 0, 0)
    raw = bytearray()
    if rgb_only:
        for y in range(canvas.h):
            raw.append(0)
            off = y * canvas.w * 4
            for x in range(canvas.w):
                i = off + x * 4
                raw.extend(canvas.p[i : i + 3])
    else:
        for y in range(canvas.h):
            raw.append(0)
            off = y * canvas.w * 4
            raw.extend(canvas.p[off : off + canvas.w * 4])
    return b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr) + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(bytes(raw), 6)) + chunk(b"IEND", b"")

def rgb_hex(col: Color) -> str:
    return f"#{col[0]:02x}{col[1]:02x}{col[2]:02x}"


def parse_background(opts: ParsedOptions) -> Tuple[Color, bool]:
    """Return background and whether RGB output is sufficient."""
    if opts.has("transparent"):
        return TRANSPARENT, False
    bg = opts.first("background")
    if bg and len(bg) == 6:
        return (int(bg[0:2], 16), int(bg[2:4], 16), int(bg[4:6], 16), 255), True
    if bg and len(bg) == 8:
        # The reference creates an ARGB image with a transparent initial background.
        return TRANSPARENT, False
    return WHITE, True


def shape_points(shape: Shape, model: DiagramModel, offset: float = 0.0) -> List[Tuple[float, float]]:
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = shape_bounds(shape, model)
    x1 += offset; y1 += offset; x2 += offset; y2 += offset
    w = x2 - x1
    if shape.kind == "decision":
        return [((x1 + x2) / 2, y1), (x2, (y1 + y2) / 2), ((x1 + x2) / 2, y2), (x1, (y1 + y2) / 2)]
    if shape.kind == "io":
        sl = min(w * 0.18, model.cw * 1.5)
        return [(x1 + sl, y1), (x2, y1), (x2 - sl, y2), (x1, y2)]
    if shape.kind == "trapezoid":
        sl = min(w * 0.18, model.cw * 1.5)
        return [(x1 + sl, y1), (x2 - sl, y1), (x2, y2), (x1, y2)]
    if shape.kind == "manual":
        sl = min(w * 0.20, model.cw * 2.0)
        return [(x1 + sl, y1), (x2, y1), (x2, y2), (x1, y2)]
    return [(x1, y1), (x1, y2), (x2, y2), (x2, y1)]


def draw_shape(canvas: Canvas, shape: Shape, model: DiagramModel, opts: ParsedOptions, shadow: bool = False) -> None:
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = shape_bounds(shape, model)
    offset = 5.0 if shadow else 0.0
    fill = (128, 128, 128, 120) if shadow else shape.fill
    stroke = (128, 128, 128, 180) if shadow else BLACK
    sw = max(1.0, model.scale)
    if shape.dashed and not shadow:
        fill = None  # dashed shapes are outlines in the reference
    if shadow and shape.dashed:
        return
    kind = shape.kind
    if kind == "ellipse":
        canvas.ellipse((x1 + x2) / 2 + offset, (y1 + y2) / 2 + offset, abs(x2 - x1) / 2, abs(y2 - y1) / 2, fill, stroke if not shadow else None, sw)
    elif kind == "storage":
        pts = shape_points(shape, model, offset)
        canvas.polygon(pts, fill, stroke if not shadow else None, sw, False)
        if not shadow:
            canvas.ellipse((x1 + x2) / 2, y1, abs(x2 - x1) / 2, max(2, model.ch * 0.30), None, BLACK, sw)
            canvas.line(x1, y1, x1, y2, BLACK, sw)
            canvas.line(x2, y1, x2, y2, BLACK, sw)
            # bottom arc approximation
            canvas.ellipse((x1 + x2) / 2, y2, abs(x2 - x1) / 2, max(2, model.ch * 0.35), None, BLACK, sw)
    elif kind == "document":
        pts = [(x1 + offset, y1 + offset), (x2 + offset, y1 + offset), (x2 + offset, y2 - model.ch * 0.25 + offset), ((x1 + x2) / 2 + offset, y2 + offset), (x1 + offset, y2 - model.ch * 0.25 + offset)]
        canvas.polygon(pts, fill, stroke if not shadow else None, sw, shape.dashed)
    elif opts.has("round-corners") and kind == "rect":
        # Simple rounded rectangle: fill main body and draw outline with quarter arcs approximated by many points.
        r = min(model.cw * 0.6, abs(x2 - x1) / 3, abs(y2 - y1) / 3)
        pts: List[Tuple[float, float]] = []
        for cx, cy, a0, a1 in [(x1 + r, y1 + r, math.pi, 1.5 * math.pi), (x2 - r, y1 + r, 1.5 * math.pi, 2 * math.pi), (x2 - r, y2 - r, 0, 0.5 * math.pi), (x1 + r, y2 - r, 0.5 * math.pi, math.pi)]:
            for i in range(6):
                a = a0 + (a1 - a0) * i / 5
                pts.append((cx + offset + r * math.cos(a), cy + offset + r * math.sin(a)))
        canvas.polygon(pts, fill, stroke if not shadow else None, sw, shape.dashed)
    else:
        canvas.polygon(shape_points(shape, model, offset), fill, stroke if not shadow else None, sw, shape.dashed)


def draw_arrow(canvas: Canvas, arrow: Arrow, model: DiagramModel) -> None:
    x, y = arrow.x, arrow.y
    sx = max(4.0, model.cw * 0.5)
    sy = max(5.0, model.ch * 0.5)
    if arrow.direction == ">":
        pts = [(x - sx, y - sy), (x + sx, y), (x - sx, y + sy)]
    elif arrow.direction == "<":
        pts = [(x + sx, y - sy), (x - sx, y), (x + sx, y + sy)]
    elif arrow.direction == "^":
        pts = [(x, y - sy), (x - sx, y + sy), (x + sx, y + sy)]
    else:  # v
        pts = [(x - sx, y - sy), (x + sx, y - sy), (x, y + sy)]
    canvas.polygon(pts, BLACK, None)


def render_png(text: str, opts: ParsedOptions) -> bytes:
    model = analyse_diagram(text, opts)
    bg, rgb_only = parse_background(opts)
    canvas = Canvas(model.width, model.height, bg)
    # Shadows and filled shapes first.
    if not opts.has("no-shadows"):
        for s in model.shapes:
            draw_shape(canvas, s, model, opts, shadow=True)
    for s in model.shapes:
        draw_shape(canvas, s, model, opts, shadow=False)
    sw = max(1.0, model.scale)
    for seg in model.segs:
        canvas.line(seg.x1, seg.y1, seg.x2, seg.y2, BLACK, sw, seg.dashed)
    for arrow in model.arrows:
        draw_arrow(canvas, arrow, model)
    for mark in model.markers:
        canvas.disk(mark.x, mark.y, max(2.5, 3.5 * model.scale), WHITE)
        canvas.line(mark.x - 3.5 * model.scale, mark.y, mark.x + 3.5 * model.scale, mark.y, BLACK, sw)
        canvas.line(mark.x, mark.y - 3.5 * model.scale, mark.x, mark.y + 3.5 * model.scale, BLACK, sw)
    # Text
    font_pix = max(1, int(round(2 * model.scale)))
    font_h = 7 * font_pix
    for tr in model.texts:
        x = int(2 * model.cw + tr.col * model.cw + max(1, int(model.cw * 0.20)))
        y = int((2 + tr.row) * model.ch + max(0, (model.ch - font_h) // 2))
        canvas.text(x, y, tr.text, tr.color, model.scale)
    if model.debug:
        dbg = (200, 200, 200, 180)
        for c in range(model.cols + 1):
            x = (2 + c) * model.cw
            canvas.line(x, 2 * model.ch, x, (2 + model.rows) * model.ch, dbg, 1, False)
        for r in range(model.rows + 1):
            y = (2 + r) * model.ch
            canvas.line(2 * model.cw, y, (2 + model.cols) * model.cw, y, dbg, 1, False)
    return png_bytes(canvas, rgb_only)

def fmtf(x: float) -> str:

def path_for_shape(shape: Shape, model: DiagramModel, round_corners: bool = False) -> str:
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = shape_bounds(shape, model)
    if shape.kind == "ellipse":
        # cubic approximation
        cx, cy = (x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2
        rx, ry = (x2 - x1) / 2, (y2 - y1) / 2
        k = 0.5522847498
        return f"M{fmtf(cx+rx)} {fmtf(cy)} C{fmtf(cx+rx)} {fmtf(cy+k*ry)} {fmtf(cx+k*rx)} {fmtf(cy+ry)} {fmtf(cx)} {fmtf(cy+ry)} C{fmtf(cx-k*rx)} {fmtf(cy+ry)} {fmtf(cx-rx)} {fmtf(cy+k*ry)} {fmtf(cx-rx)} {fmtf(cy)} C{fmtf(cx-rx)} {fmtf(cy-k*ry)} {fmtf(cx-k*rx)} {fmtf(cy-ry)} {fmtf(cx)} {fmtf(cy-ry)} C{fmtf(cx+k*rx)} {fmtf(cy-ry)} {fmtf(cx+rx)} {fmtf(cy-k*ry)} {fmtf(cx+rx)} {fmtf(cy)} z"
    if shape.kind == "storage":
        return f"M{fmtf(x1)} {fmtf(y1)} C{fmtf(x1+(x2-x1)/6)} {fmtf(y1+model.ch/2)} {fmtf(x2-(x2-x1)/6)} {fmtf(y1+model.ch/2)} {fmtf(x2)} {fmtf(y1)} C{fmtf(x2-(x2-x1)/6)} {fmtf(y1-model.ch/2)} {fmtf(x1+(x2-x1)/6)} {fmtf(y1-model.ch/2)} {fmtf(x1)} {fmtf(y1)} M{fmtf(x1)} {fmtf(y1)} L{fmtf(x1)} {fmtf(y2)} C{fmtf(x1+(x2-x1)/6)} {fmtf(y2+model.ch/2)} {fmtf(x2-(x2-x1)/6)} {fmtf(y2+model.ch/2)} {fmtf(x2)} {fmtf(y2)} L{fmtf(x2)} {fmtf(y1)} "
    if shape.kind == "document":
        yy = y2 - model.ch * 0.25
        return f"M{fmtf(x1)} {fmtf(y1)} L{fmtf(x2)} {fmtf(y1)} L{fmtf(x2)} {fmtf(yy)} Q{fmtf((x1+x2)*0.65)} {fmtf(y2-model.ch*0.45)} {fmtf((x1+x2)/2)} {fmtf(yy)} Q{fmtf((x1+x2)*0.35)} {fmtf(y2+model.ch*0.15)} {fmtf(x1)} {fmtf(yy)} z"
    if round_corners and shape.kind == "rect":
        r = min(model.cw * 0.5, (x2 - x1) / 3, (y2 - y1) / 3)
        return f"M{fmtf(x1+r)} {fmtf(y1)} Q{fmtf(x1)} {fmtf(y1)} {fmtf(x1)} {fmtf(y1+r)} L{fmtf(x1)} {fmtf(y2-r)} Q{fmtf(x1)} {fmtf(y2)} {fmtf(x1+r)} {fmtf(y2)} L{fmtf(x2-r)} {fmtf(y2)} Q{fmtf(x2)} {fmtf(y2)} {fmtf(x2)} {fmtf(y2-r)} L{fmtf(x2)} {fmtf(y1+r)} Q{fmtf(x2)} {fmtf(y1)} {fmtf(x2-r)} {fmtf(y1)} L{fmtf(x1+r)} {fmtf(y1)} z"
    pts = shape_points(shape, model)
    return "M" + " L".join(f"{fmtf(x)} {fmtf(y)}" for x, y in pts) + " z"

    out.append("")
    out.append("")

def default_output_for_input(inp: str, svg: bool) -> str:
    ext = ".svg" if svg else ".png"
    d = os.path.dirname(inp)
    base = os.path.basename(inp)
    idx = base.rfind(".")
    root = base[:idx] if idx >= 0 else base
    out = os.path.join(d, root + ext)
    if os.path.exists(out):
        n = 2
        while True:
            cand = os.path.join(d, f"{root}_{n}{ext}")
            if not os.path.exists(cand):
                return cand
            n += 1
    return out


def default_html_output(inp: str) -> str:
    d = os.path.dirname(inp)
    base = os.path.basename(inp)
    idx = base.rfind(".")
    root = base[:idx] if idx >= 0 else base
    return os.path.join(d, root + "_processed.html")


def print_run_header(parsed: ParsedOptions) -> None:
    sys.stdout.write(VERSION_BANNER + "\n")
    sys.stdout.write("Running with options:\n")
    for line in option_lines(parsed):
        sys.stdout.write(line + "\n")


def render_bytes(text: str, parsed: ParsedOptions) -> bytes:
    return render_svg(text, parsed) if parsed.has("svg") else render_png(text, parsed)


def read_text_file(path: str, encoding: str) -> str:
    with open(path, "r", encoding=encoding, errors="strict", newline=None) as f:
        return f.read()


def write_output(path: str, data: bytes) -> bool:
    try:
        parent = os.path.dirname(path)
        if parent and not os.path.isdir(parent):
            return False
        if os.path.isdir(path):
            return False
        with open(path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


def run_render(parsed: ParsedOptions) -> int:
    inp = parsed.positionals[0]
    out = parsed.positionals[1] if len(parsed.positionals) > 1 else None
    output_stdout = False
    if out is None:
        if inp == "-":
            out = "-"
        else:
            out = default_output_for_input(inp, parsed.has("svg"))
    if out == "-":
        output_stdout = True

    encoding = parsed.first("encoding", "UTF-8") or "UTF-8"

    if output_stdout:
        # Quiet filter mode.
        try:
            if inp == "-":
                data_in = sys.stdin.buffer.read().decode(encoding)
            else:
                data_in = read_text_file(inp, encoding)
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(render_bytes(data_in, parsed))
            return 0
        except Exception as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {e}\n")
            return 1

    print_run_header(parsed)
    if inp == "-":
        sys.stdout.write("Reading standard input\n")
        try:
            data_in = sys.stdin.buffer.read().decode(encoding)
        except Exception as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {e}\n")
            return 1
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(f"Reading file: {inp}\n")
        if not os.path.isfile(inp):
            sys.stderr.write(f"Error: File {inp} does not exist\n")
            return 1
        try:
            data_in = read_text_file(inp, encoding)
        except Exception as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {e}\n")
            return 1
    sys.stdout.write(f"Rendering to file: {out}\n")
    try:
        data = render_bytes(data_in, parsed)
    except ZeroDivisionError:
        sys.stderr.write('Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ArithmeticException: / by zero\n')
        sys.stderr.write('\tat org.stathissideris.ascii2image.text.TextGrid.fixTabs(TextGrid.java:1619)\n')
        sys.stderr.write('\tat org.stathissideris.ascii2image.text.TextGrid.initialiseWithLines(TextGrid.java:1542)\n')
        sys.stderr.write('\tat org.stathissideris.ascii2image.text.TextGrid.loadFrom(TextGrid.java:1518)\n')
        sys.stderr.write('\tat org.stathissideris.ascii2image.core.CommandLineConverter.main(CommandLineConverter.java:233)\n')
        return 1
    except Exception as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {e}\n")
        return 1
    if not write_output(out, data):
        sys.stderr.write(f"Error: Cannot write to file {out}\n")
        return 1
    sys.stdout.write("Done in 0sec\n")
    return 0


def parse_pre_attrs(attr: str) -> Optional[str]:
    # Return id (or None) if class contains textdiagram; otherwise sentinel "" for no match.
    cls_m = re.search(r"\bclass\s*=\s*(['\"])(.*?)\1", attr, re.I | re.S)
    if not cls_m or "textdiagram" not in cls_m.group(2).split():
        return ""
    id_m = re.search(r"\bid\s*=\s*(['\"])(.*?)\1", attr, re.I | re.S)
    return id_m.group(2) if id_m else None
